chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever does not have his offering (hady) with him and performs Hajj al-Ifrad with a preference over Hajj al-Tamattu', he has preferred (disliked) the religion of Allah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All these narrations indicate that the obligatory duty upon the accountable person in Hajj is Tamattu' rather than Ifrad and Qiran. Therefore, whoever performs Ifrad or Qiran while having the ability to perform Tamattu', that does not suffice him as the Hajj of Islam. We said this because these narrations contain the command to perform Tamattu'; so whoever does not perform Tamattu' has not done what he was commanded to do. And because they (the Imams) attributed the practice of Tamattu' to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah, and the practice of other forms to opinions and desires. And every action that contradicts the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) does not suffice for what Allah Almighty imposed upon the people. Furthermore, they have clarified in some of the narrations we presented earlier that Ifrad in Hajj is from the opinion of Umar, and the saying of Umar is not a proof in Islamic jurisprudence. They also mentioned that they do not know for Allah any Hajj other than Tamattu'. This phrase indicates that whoever does not perform Tamattu' while having the ability, it does not suffice him as the Hajj of Islam. As for when the state is one of necessity and he is not able to perform Tamattu' therein, then there is no harm in restricting himself to Qiran and Ifrad. This indicates that.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Hajj al-Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.الْإِقْرَانُ: Hajj al-Qiran (combining Umrah and Hajj together)
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: The sacrificial animal offered during Hajj
key_terms.رَأْيُ عُمَرَ: The opinion of Umar ibn al-Khattab

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Hajj al-Tamattu', Ifrad, and Qiran in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights that Hajj al-Tamattu' is the preferred and obligatory form for those capable, as narrations attribute it directly to the Quran and Sunnah, whereas Ifrad and Qiran are linked to human opinion, specifically Umar's view. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on following the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation over the companions' juristic reasoning, though Ifrad or Qiran remain valid in cases of necessity or inability to perform Tamattu'.
